analysis:
This PR adds only documentation and a changelog entry. The changelog (changelog.d/ssd-retirement-in-slices.md:1-9) and the docs table row at docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md:377 describe a behavior change in the provider's SSD prefix-cache owned retirement: TTL and disk-budget sweeps now remove 16 files per hold of the removal lock and epoch barrier (SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.filesPerSlice, removeInSlices) instead of the whole batch. Each hold rechecks ownership, and a refusal ends the batch. The implementation is not in the supplied evidence, so I could not verify it.

Security relevance, under T-041 and TB-007: the described change targets availability and latency. Cache hits on the submit thread and donor index publication no longer block on long sweeps. The documented controls are unchanged: the 30-minute sliding TTL, the LRU disk budget, HMAC-keyed names, per-file AES-GCM, and the epoch not rotating on per-file removals. Slicing could briefly interleave other operations between slices. The documentation says ownership is rechecked per slice, the busy-lease skip is retained, and the survivor identity and sequence are unchanged. Epoch-record read failure handling (line 378) is unchanged. Slicing delays TTL expiry only slightly (up to 12% longer sweeps), which does not extend the accepted TTL window enough to need a fresh SEC-035 sign-off.

No findings. The remaining question for the code pass is whether removeInSlices correctly rechecks epoch, binding and closed-store state between slices, and whether the retirement lease semantics hold across slice boundaries. That code is outside this batch.
